title: gemini-cli installations done through brew having Keychain perpetually unavailable

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue clearly reports a functional bug where gemini-cli installed via Homebrew cannot access or store sensitive extension variables in the macOS Keychain, defaulting to file storage, whereas npm-installed versions work properly.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: Investigating platform-specific native module binding issues (@github/keytar), macOS codesign/entitlement differences, and Homebrew vs NPM installation paths requires testing across packaged environments on macOS.

summary.problem: gemini-cli installed via Homebrew fails to load or access the macOS Keychain via @github/keytar, falling back to FileKeychain.
summary.root_cause: Homebrew-installed gemini-cli packages or standalone binary distributions either fail to bundle/resolve the native @github/keytar .node addon or fail macOS Keychain security default-keychain checks in non-NPM execution contexts.
summary.context: NPM installations run within a node_modules environment where native modules resolve normally, whereas Homebrew builds or binary bundles rely on staged native modules or specific runtime path resolution.

steps: Update loadKeychainModule in packages/core/src/services/keychainService.ts to support fallback native module resolution for packaged distributions when standard ESM import of @github/keytar fails.
Enhance error logging and diagnostic messaging in getNativeKeychain to report specific native addon loading or initialization errors.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: KeychainService properly attempts native module loading with fallbacks and provides detailed debug log messages when native keychain bindings are missing or fail to initialize.
verification_steps: Add unit test cases in packages/core/src/services/keychainService.test.ts to verify module import failure handling.
Verify that isUsingFileFallback correctly returns true when native keychain bindings cannot be resolved.
